extracted.intended_audience: college composition instructors, writing researchers, and education researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of the effects of one-half semester of news writing instruction in an English Composition I course on students' writing performance and attitudes, using pre/post tests, a questionnaire (including the Geer Fear Survey), and holistic essay grading. The study compares a treatment group to three traditional control groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anxiety
rubrics_metrics.description: Students' level of writing anxiety was measured as one of the outcome factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured pre- and post-semester; reported as one of seven factors examined. The questionnaire included the Geer Fear Survey components that assess anxiety-related aspects of students' writing attitudes. Study found no significant difference between treatment and control groups on this factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Students' self-assessment of their writing ability was measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed via the questionnaire (including items from the Geer Fear Survey) on pre- and post-tests. Used to judge perceived ability; no significant difference found between groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Students' motivation to write was measured as an attitudinal outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured through the questionnaire/Geer Fear Survey on pre- and post-semester tests. Intended to capture changes in motivation attributable to instructional approach; study found no significant effect of news-writing instruction on motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitude
rubrics_metrics.description: General student attitudes toward writing and the writing course were measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included within the questionnaire/Geer Fear Survey administered before and after the semester. Used to evaluate whether news-writing instruction affects attitudes; no significant group differences reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar and mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective writing mechanics (grammar, usage, mechanics) were evaluated as part of writing performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed via the essay portion of pre- and post-tests and graded by instructors using a holistic grading scale. No significant difference between treatment and control groups was found for grammar and mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall writing skills (as demonstrated in the writing exercise/essay) were evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essay portions of the tests were graded holistically by writing instructors to capture writing performance. Despite the treatment, the study reported no significant difference between groups on this dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception of practicality (practicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students' perception of the practicality of the writing instruction for work after college (practicability) was measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the questionnaire/Geer Fear Survey; unlike the other six factors, results revealed a significant difference—students in the news-writing treatment perceived the instruction as more practical for post-college work. This is an attitudinal/perceived utility measure rather than an objective skills measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic grading scale for essay evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a holistic grading scale by writing instructors to grade the essay portion of pre- and post-tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructors applied a holistic rubric to score essays, which served as the primary instrument for measuring writing performance (writing skills, grammar/mechanics). The study reports outcomes based on these holistic scores.
